# Rules for each kind of content

Matteo reviewed these in the tone check on 29 Oct 2026. Where he added to a rule, his words are in. Where he left a rule blank, it stands as drafted.

All of them sit on top of `voice.md` and `compliance.md`. `matteo/thinking.md` shows how he builds each kind.

## Slides and decks

- One message per slide, written as a full-sentence title.
- One big number at most per slide.
- A source line on every slide with data.
- Ink title slide, white content slides. Start from the deck template (`links.md`).
- Investor and partner decks follow the same standards for evidence, product mechanics and risk. Change the depth and emphasis for the audience, not the standards.

## Company posts on X and LinkedIn

- The point or the number first, then two or three short lines, then the view.
- No hashtags. Emoji and exclamation marks only when they fit. The account says "we".
- LinkedIn: up to 250 words when the post explains an argument; about 100 words for an update, which is the preference.
- Live prices from the app, if possible as dated, time-stamped screenshots with the market and quote units visible. Never a hint that a quote guarantees execution, liquidity or a return. Never a gain (house rule).

## Matteo's own posts

- His voice and "I". Personal opinion kept apart from company facts.
- The same standards for numbers, product claims and risk wording as company posts.
- The agreed product language, used the same way every time.

## Newsletter

- Lead with the news and explain why it matters.
- Cover difficulty markets, trading activity and network hashrate.
- Link the sources and date every estimate.
- A factual subject line.
- State a publishing cadence only when the team has committed to one.
- Include the relevant risk context whenever an issue discusses positions.
- Signed Doefin. A piece that gives a personal view names its author.

## Glossary

- A plain, factual definition under 160 characters, with no product language.
- Then a longer explanation and one worked example.
- For a measure, say what it is not as well as what it is ("not a live measurement of mining activity").

## Research notes and articles

- State the main finding early.
- Give every figure its source, date, units and method.
- Keep observations, estimates, forecasts and opinion apart, and label each. The website's source badges (Measured, Single source, Judgement, Illustrative) still apply to each figure.
- Explain the assumptions and any material uncertainty.
- Assess forecast hits and misses with the same method, and make material misses and corrections visible.

## Help docs

- "You", short steps, one task per page.
- A warning comes before the step it affects.
- Explain a rule rather than describing the wait ("Yes wins if the difficulty at that block is at or above the threshold").

## Tool text

- Say what the tool estimates.
- Label every input with its unit, and show the assumptions.
- Explain the result in plain language, and keep BTC production apart from revenue and profit.
- Call outputs estimates, and show their material limitations next to the result.

## Emails to partners and investors

- Open with the reason for writing, give the context they need, and end with one clear ask.
- An update can follow Matteo's order: (1) what happened, and deal flow; (2) what I am thinking; (3) the idea or next steps; (4) product updates, if any; (5) the ask.
- Signed with a first name.

## Announcements

- What changed, for whom and from when.
- No "thrilled" and no "game-changing". A claim like "first" needs proof on file.

## App text

- Buttons start with a verb. The app button on the website says "Enter app".
- Errors say what happened and what to do next.
- Confirmations repeat the button's words.
